subject: Future Tech
title: Why Classical Computers Hit Walls
description: A quick, practical guide to Why Classical Computers Hit Walls.

hook.text: Classical computers double power roughly every two years, but some problems grow faster than any chip can keep up.

buildup.text: Factoring a 300-digit number would take a classical supercomputer longer than the age of the universe.

discovery.text: These are exponential problems. Each added digit multiplies the work, making brute force hopeless.

twist.text: Quantum computers attack exponential problems differently, using superposition to explore many paths at once.

climax.text: A future quantum machine could factor that 300-digit number in hours, breaking today's encryption.

quiz.question: Why can't classical computers efficiently factor very large numbers?
